facts.statement: The genus Chinchenia was first described by Young in 1965.
Chinchenia is an extinct basal pistosauroid from the Middle Triassic of Guizhou Province in southwestern China.
facts.quote: Chinchenia is an extinct genus of a basal pistosauroid known from the Middle Triassic (possibly Ladinian age) of Guizhou Province, southwestern China.

facts.statement: The genus is known from at least four extremely fragmentary individuals that were preserved and collected together.
facts.quote: Chinchenia is known from at least 4 extremely fragmentary individuals all preserved and collected together.

facts.statement: The lectotype specimen is IVPP V3227, consisting of the front end of the left mandible.
facts.quote: The lectotype of Chinchenia was chosen to be IVPP V3227, the front end of the left mandible

facts.statement: Paratype material includes parts of the jaw with teeth, numerous vertebrae, ribs, shoulder bones, arm bones, leg bones, and a fibula fragment.
facts.quote: Other elements from its original description are considered to be paratypes and include the front part of a left lower jaw with 5 broken teeth, 11 neck, six lower back and one sacral vertebrae in various degrees of completeness, 8 unidentified neural arch fragments, many fragments of dorsal and sacral ribs including one proximal part of a left dorsal rib, two right scapulae one of which is very incomplete, two complete humeri, 5 incomplete humeri of which four are distal ends and one is proximal, two complete thigh bones, a proximal and a distal tibiae, and a fibula fragment.

facts.statement: All known Chinchenia specimens are housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: All specimens are housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.

facts.statement: The fossils were collected near the Cangxi Bridge at Shangpu, Tsanchichiao, 7 km west of Qingzhen in Guizhou Province.
facts.quote: The material was collected near the Cangxi Bridge at Shangpu, Tsanchichiao, 7 km west of Qingzhen of Guizhou Province.

facts.statement: While originally attributed to the Anisian Guangling Formation, subsequent authors considered a Ladinian age more likely for the material.
facts.quote: Although originally said to come from the first member of the Anisian Guangling Formation, a Ladinian age was considered more likely by subsequent authors for the material.

facts.statement: Chinchenia is classified as a basal pistosauroid.
facts.quote: Chinchenia is an extinct genus of a basal pistosauroid

facts.statement: The parent group of Chinchenia is Pistosauroidea.
Chinchenia is classified within the class Reptilia.
Chinchenia was named by Yang Zhongjian, also known as Chung-Chien Young, in 1965.
facts.quote: Chinchenia was first described and named by Yang Zhongjian, also known as Chung-Chien Young, in 1965

rejected.statement: The generic name Chinchenia is derived from Chinchen, an alternative spelling of the city of Qingzhen where the holotype was found.
rejected.quote: The generic name is derived from Chinchen, an alternative spelling of the city of Qingzhen where the holotype was found.
